justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are met: Claim Submission Module serves customers/brokers (R-01), Adjuster Dashboard & Case Workspace serves adjusters (R-02), and Claim Routing Engine in the Migration Router enables claim-type-by-claim-type migration (R-03).
justifications.performance_efficiency: Azure Cache for Redis, Optimistic UI Manager, and Async Polling / WebSocket Notifier decouple adjuster screens from 5-second mainframe latency to achieve sub-2s loads (R-05). However, explicit throttling mechanisms for the fixed nightly batch window are omitted.
justifications.compatibility: The Mainframe Integration Adapter (Legacy Protocol Client, IBM MQ) and Translation Service effectively coexist with the legacy COBOL/DB2 system. However, specific architectural elements handling the scheduled batch file window integration remain somewhat generic.
justifications.usability: Both user personas have tailored interfaces: Claim Submission Module offers wizard-style flows with Offline Draft Storage for external users, while Adjuster Dashboard & Case Workspace provides an optimized operational interface for claims adjusters.
justifications.reliability: Transactional Outbox Store, Dual-Write & Reconciliation Manager, Dead-Letter Subsystems, and Resiliency & Circuit Breaker Component (Polly) explicitly ensure zero data loss, fault tolerance, and idempotency to satisfy R-04.
justifications.security: R-07 is fully satisfied via Auth Client (MSAL.js) and Authentication Middleware federating with Active Directory using OIDC/OAuth2. Data integrity and accountability are reinforced through the Audit Log Store and Audit & Reconciliation Logger.
justifications.maintainability: The Fallback & Feature Flag Manager combined with the Claim Routing Engine provides dynamic toggling to switch claim types back to the mainframe within one day (R-06). Clear separation exists between domain logic and legacy adapters.
justifications.portability: The architecture addresses the hybrid topology (Azure West Europe and on-premise mainframe) effectively, though heavy reliance on proprietary Azure services (Azure Container Apps, Service Bus, Redis) poses vendor lock-in considerations for a cloud-inexperienced team.

PERF-01.justification: Redis caching, distributed response caching at the BFF, and asynchronous WebSocket updates enable adjuster screens to render cached data in under 2 seconds while background fetching hydrates mainframe records.
sensitivity_points: Cache hit ratios and TTL configuration in Redis
WebSocket connection stability for client updates
tradeoffs: Caching risks eventual consistency against changing mainframe data

PERF-02.justification: Peak claim submissions are captured asynchronously into Azure Service Bus and transactional outbox stores, rate-limiting downstream message delivery to prevent mainframe overload during the fixed batch window.
sensitivity_points: Queue depth capacity and rate-limiting throttles on the adapter
tradeoffs: Asynchronous message buffering delays final claim confirmation on mainframe

AVAIL-01.justification: Submissions persist locally in Azure SQL via the transactional outbox pattern and queue in Service Bus; circuit breakers pause mainframe delivery until the batch window completes without data loss.
sensitivity_points: Service Bus queue storage limits during extended downtime
tradeoffs: Extended buffering increases latency before mainframe state is updated

AVAIL-02.justification: Dual-Write & Reconciliation Manager, Dead-Letter Queues, and the Migration Sync Tracker record transaction states and detect partial sync failures, ensuring safe replay and duplicate prevention.
sensitivity_points: Idempotency key enforcement across legacy integration boundaries
Reconciliation cadence and automated error detection
tradeoffs: Dual-write reconciliation logic adds operational and processing overhead

MOD-01.justification: The Migration Router ACL isolates legacy models using feature flags via Azure App Configuration, allowing per-claim-type dynamic routing and instantaneous switch-back without modifying mainframe programs.
sensitivity_points: Dynamic flag evaluation latency in the routing pipeline
Accuracy of translation mapping for legacy formats
tradeoffs: Maintaining dual routing paths temporarily increases codebase complexity

MOD-02.justification: The frontend is fully decoupled from the mainframe by the API Gateway and Migration Router; decommissioning the mainframe only requires repointing the routing engine, leaving user interfaces unchanged.
sensitivity_points: Strict isolation between UI layer and backend integration protocols
tradeoffs: Maintaining abstraction layers incurs persistent architectural complexity

SEC-01.justification: Authentication middleware and MSAL enforce AD identity, and audit logging captures security activity. However, broker-level tenancy segregation and fine-grained authorization policies are not explicitly detailed in the component model.
sensitivity_points: Token claim validation logic for broker-customer ownership rules
tradeoffs: Centralized authorization checks at BFF increase processing per request

SEC-02.justification: SSO via Active Directory using OIDC/OAuth2 cuts off adjuster access to the modernization platform immediately upon account deactivation; however, automated revocation propagation to legacy mainframe credentials lacks explicit architectural definition.
sensitivity_points: Token lifespan and revocation check intervals across session boundaries
tradeoffs: Short-lived access tokens require frequent token refreshes
